messages.subject: correlation matrix
parts:
Hi all,

I'm attempting to plot a correlation matrix similar to (but not
precisely replicating) the one found here:
http://addictedtor.free.fr/graphiques/RGraphGallery.php?graph=152

I think the continuous color is redundant to the continuous size, so I
think I'll just go with black for negative correlations and white for
positive correlations. Below is my attempt in ggplot, but I'm having
trouble:

1. ensuring size defines the *area* of the circle

2. ensuring the size of a point reflecting a correlation of 1 is such
that is just touches the bounds of its bin (i.e., if it's in row1, it
spans from 0.5 to 1.5 on the x-axis)


library(ggplot2)

mat = matrix(rnorm(100),10,10)

ggplot(
melt(cor(mat))
,aes(
x=X1
,y=X2
,size=abs(value)
,colour=I(ifelse(value>0,'white','black'))
)
)+
geom_point()+
scale_colour_manual(values=c('white','black'))+
labs(
y=''
,x=''
)+
opts(
panel.grid.minor = theme_blank()
,panel.grid.major = theme_blank()
,legend.position = 'none'
,axis.text.x = theme_text(hjust=1,angle=90)
)


--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology
Dalhousie University

parts:
Interesting plan, I'd probably use something like this, although white
for +ve correlation doesn't quite seem right.

scale_area() seems relevant, combined with the to parameter, I seem to
be able to get close with

+ scale_area(to=c(0,23))

but I have no idea why 23ish is the right factor there ...

--J

On Tue, Apr 14, 2009 at 3:50 PM, James Howison
<ja...@freelancepropaganda.com> wrote:
>
> Interesting plan, I'd probably use something like this, although white
> for +ve correlation doesn't quite seem right.
>
> scale_area() seems relevant, combined with the to parameter, I seem to
> be able to get close with
>
> + scale_area(to=c(0,23))
>
> but I have no idea why 23ish is the right factor there ...

The problem is trying to match up the scale of the points (measured in
mm) to the scale of the plot (which can be any arbitrary size). To
solve this problem you really need a circle geom that operates
entirely with data units (i.e. the circles would radius 1 data unit),
but it's not obvious to me what generality this geom should have:

* should you specify just the radius, or should it be possible to
draw ovals as will?
* if it should, how should they be parameterised? with
variance-covariance matrix?

It's probably not really a lot of work, but I haven't had time to
think about it properly.

Hadley
